higher_level_requirement: The Bootstrap Monitor of the DPU-BOOT CSC shall provide the capability to download configurations of the DPU-RTOS from the RS-232 interface to EEPROM on command.

Each task has an expected execution frequency, and if a task does not execute as expected, an error is reported in DPU housekeeping. higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall maintain counts of both the number of commands successfully received and rejected and report the parameters in DPU_HK.

label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes the higher-level requirement by specifying that memory-test results are used to exclude DRAM segments with bit errors from the VxWorks system memory pool. higher_level_requirement: The DPU-EDAC shall contain a background task which walks DRAM to trip single-bit errors (SBEs).
lower_level_requirement: DRAM BITPart of the memory is tested in Boot Sequence 1, and part of the memory is tested during Boot Sequence 2. During Boot Sequence 1, ? KB of DRAM is tested before the Bootstrap is copied to this area. During Boot Sequence 2, the remaining memory is tested in ? KB blocks. The DRAM BIT first writes the address of each word in a block to that word in the block. Then the test flushes the cache and reads back the entire block. If a single-bit error occurs on the read-back, the location is read again. If another single-bit error occurs, the test assumes a hard error and marks the whole block bad. If a multiple-bit error occurs, the whole block is marked bad. If the value read back does not match the address, the whole block is marked bad. This same process is repeated with the ones complement of the address. The Bootstrap stores the results of the DRAM BIT in EEPROM as a series of x consecutive y-bit words. Each bit in a result word represents the result of testing a ? KB block of DRAM. These bits are mapped to DRAM by proceeding from least-significant bit (LSb) to most-significant bit (MSb) as the addresses of the memory blocks increase. A set bit indicates that a block of DRAM has failed. A clear bit indicates that a block of DRAM has passed the test.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement defines a DRAM built-in test that systematically walks memory blocks, writes patterns, flushes cache, and reads them back to detect single-bit and multiple-bit errors. Its handling of repeated single-bit read-back errors and marking affected blocks bad directly operationalizes the higher-level objective of walking DRAM to expose SBEs. Although it is described in boot sequences rather than explicitly as a background task, the core required behavior of traversing DRAM to trip/detect SBEs is refined by the detailed test procedure.
